full_judgment: 12. It will be necessary to narrate in brief the facts and circumstances of the case under which respondent No. 2, Raquibuddin Ahmed filed the Contempt petition against the appellant and another. Respondent No. 2 filed Title Suit No. 697 of 1985 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Bangladesh Shipping Corporation and the Ministry of Shipping for declaration that the order of termination of his service dated 31-8-82 was illegal, void and for a direction on the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation, briefly, BSC, to reinstate him in his service as the Secretary of the said Corporation with all financial benefits. The said suit was decreed on 22-6-89, against which BSC preferred an appeal being, Title Appeal No. 223 of 1989 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka. The said appeal was dismissed and the decree of the trial Court was affirmed on 17-2-91. Thereafter BSC preferred Civil Revision No. 1380 of 1991. The said revision case was discharged on 7-4-93 and the judgment and decree of the trial Court was upheld by the High Court Division. Against the said judgment, BSC filed a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 286 of 1993 before the Appellate Division. In the meanwhile, the Ministry of Shipping also filed a similar petition for leave to appeal being, Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.39 of 1994 beyond the date of limitation. In Civil Petition No. 286 of 1993 filed by BSC, leave was granted on the limited grounds, that is, to examine as to whether respondent No. 2 was entitled to arrears of salary and financial benefits for the period he was kept out of the office and to determine whether respondent No. 2 was liable to refund termination benefits already received by him.
